cleared.check: Monad: per block reconciliation of native flows with the PoolManager balance that block production wrote (lead L-658). cleared.check: Monad: netcheck.py and settlecheck.py extended to older blocks and to hooked unlocks (lead L-658). monad_scan.py read all 406,718 PoolManager logs of blocks 124691690 to 124991689 in the 100 block windows the endpoints allow (218,532 transactions). From them 1,354 transactions were traced: all 17 with an ERC-6909 Transfer to the zero address (burn), all 182 with an event on one of the 89 pools whose key names a hook (keys from 81 Initialize logs in the range and from the PositionManager), 400 of the 671 with a mint and 800 others at random. netcheck2.py keeps hooked pools and credits the hook's delta to the hook address as the source does (src/PoolManager.sol:178-183, 221-226): for swap the Swap event delta minus the caller delta the frame returned (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:285-315), for modifyLiquidity the BalanceDelta the after-liquidity hook frame returned when the hook address carries the return-delta flag (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:159-168, 215-244). settlecheck2.py is settlecheck.py on the same list.
cleared.result: All 1,905 completed unlocks that could be summed net to zero per account and currency, among them 244 operations on hooked pools, 205 of which moved a nonzero delta to the hook, 17 burns and 467 mints; one unlock with an unknown selector was skipped (raw/netcheck2.json). Dropping the hook deltas makes 74 of the 159 hooked unlocks fail, so the check sees them (raw/netcheck2-planted.json). settlecheck2.py finds no mismatch over 3,358 token settles, 328 native settles, 3,761 takes, 18 burns and 469 mints in blocks 124692446 to 124990852 (raw/settlecheck2.json). The traced set holds no settleFor and no clear.

cleared.check: Whether hooks with return-delta permissions change what the PoolManager pays out in total, which decides whether such pools can be checked from events. src/PoolManager.sol:178-183 credits hookDelta to the hook and callerDelta minus hookDelta to the caller after modifyLiquidity (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:209-244), and src/PoolManager.sol:221-226 does the same after swap (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:285-315). unlock reverts unless every account's delta is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114).
cleared.result: The two credits add up to the pool delta of the event, and both accounts must reach zero through take, settle, mint, burn or clear before unlock returns, so the PoolManager's net token flow in a completed unlock equals the sum of the pool deltas of the events, adjusted by ERC-6909 mints and burns and by clear. A hook cannot change that total; it can only move it between its own account and the caller's. analyze3.py therefore checks pools with return-delta hooks (243 transactions on Arc, 41 on Monad, 30 on Elysium, 25 on Robinhood Chain).

cleared.check: Whether clear leaves value that someone else can claim. clear (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319) lowers the caller's own positive delta to zero only when the amount equals it exactly, and moves no token. The cleared tokens stay in the PoolManager's balance.
cleared.result: A later sync records the whole balance as reserves (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), so the cleared amount is never credited to a later settler, and no function pays it out. It is lost to the caller who chose to clear it and is taken from nobody else. The 9 Polygon transactions above cleared 797 to 9,999,999,974,048 units this way.

leads.question: Which Monad transactions call settleFor or clear? 456 traced blocks and 1,354 traced transactions between blocks 124691690 and 124991689 hold none, and cycle 11 found 6 settleFor and 1 clear in 12,000. A scan of the PositionManager and router call data for the CLEAR_OR_TAKE and SETTLE actions with a recipient other than the caller would find them without tracing every block.
leads.why: settleFor credits a third party and clear credits nothing; both are paths where a compiled fault in the delta update would show, and neither has mined evidence on Monad beyond 7 calls.

leads.question: Can the keys of the 10 Avalanche pools analyze3.py set aside be read from Initialize logs over the PoolManager's whole history, and do those 10 removals pay the source's amounts?
leads.why: Avalanche has the fewest mined removals of the part one networks (275 rerun), and the analyze2.py run there did not finish.

leadResults.answer: Mined removals and fee collections were rerun on Polygon (321 transactions), BNB Smart Chain (377), Robinhood Chain (322), Elysium (270) and Avalanche (275 of 285). analyze2.py matched every transaction it took except artefacts of its balance fallback in shared blocks, and analyze3.py, which also replays swaps, donations, ERC-6909 mints and burns and other transactions of the block, matched every payout to the unit. Every difference has a cause outside the pool math: 9 Polygon transactions cleared their own delta, 7 Elysium and 1 BNB Smart Chain native legs share a block and reconcile per block, and 1 Avalanche transaction received an interest bearing token mint. No storage word differs apart from one dynamic fee set by a hook without an event. A second run by the established-l1 unit over other block windows agrees: Polygon: 302 removal and collection transactions in blocks 97,844,995 to 97,884,994, 293 exact to the unit, 9 rebalancing transactions in one JPYC pool where the caller left a dust credit behind by clear (no Transfer log, PoolManager JPYC balance unchanged across the block). BNB Smart Chain: 275 transactions in blocks 135,480,349 to 135,484,348, all exact, 3 native ones unchecked for lack of a tracer. Avalanche was added: 40 in blocks 101,116,887 to 101,267,286, all exact. Storage predicted from the source equalled storage at the block in every checked transaction. Robinhood Chain and Elysium belong to the arbitrum-family unit and were not run here.

With fee growth and crossed ticks carried through the swap step loop inside the transaction and in the rest of the block, all set-aside removals and fee collections on Monad (107 of 108, one pool key not found), MegaETH (8 of 8) and Arc (77 of 78, one block with a protocol fee change) pay the source's amounts to the unit, and the storage after the block, tick bitmap words included, matches. Planted faults in fee growth and in the bitmap are caught.

On Monad all 39 shared blocks of cycle 11's unattributed native legs and 417 older blocks reconcile to the wei between traced native flows and the producer-written PoolManager balance. Over 1,354 older transactions with all 17 burns, 182 transactions on hooked pools and 467 mints, all 1,905 completed unlocks net to zero with hook deltas credited to the hook, and settlecheck finds no mismatch. No settleFor or clear call occurs in the older range, so those two remain without new mined evidence.
